label: THOP1 / thop1-observed
training_or_assay: Human thimet oligopeptidase hydrolysis of synthetic Gly-Pro-Leu oligomers and of bradykinin, followed by HPLC (Knight, Dando and Barrett 1995, Biochem J 308:145-150)
exposure_requirement: Requires enzyme access in cytosol; location does not establish exposure
limitations: Exact-sequence lookup over one substrate series plus bradykinin, not a specificity model. The Gly-Pro-Leu oligomers are synthetic repeats, not antigenic peptides, so nothing here transfers to an arbitrary sequence. This catalog holds no reported non-cleavage for this enzyme: every resistant peptide in the source is a hydroxyproline analogue or carries an N-terminal pyroglutamate, and both are outside the canonical-peptide input type, so absence of a record here is not evidence of resistance. The source states that peptides of 18 or more residues cannot be cleaved and that hydrolysis is subject to potent competitive inhibition by the C-terminal product, so observed rates are not turnover in a cell. Whether the enzyme preparation was recombinant is not stated. Reported cleavage of a purified substrate does not establish that this enzyme controls the lifetime of any peptide in the cytosol of an antigen-presenting cell; primary reports disagree about whether mature class I epitopes are good substrates.

label: NLN / nln-observed
training_or_assay: Recombinant human neurolysin hydrolysis of a dynorphin A length series quantified by LC-MS, with peptide complexes resolved by X-ray crystallography (Karamyan, Aihara and colleagues 2024, Sci Rep 14:18420)
exposure_requirement: Requires enzyme access in cytosol; location does not establish exposure
limitations: Exact-sequence lookup over one substrate series, not a specificity model. Neurolysin and thimet oligopeptidase are closely related but are not interchangeable: they cleave neurotensin at distinct sites and their specificities can be swapped by mutating two active-site residues, so neither model's observations may be transferred to the other. Only observations made on the human enzyme are recorded; the widely cited bradykinin, enkephalin and neurotensin results come from rat or species-unspecified preparations and are deliberately excluded. The angiotensin I record is read from electron density in a crystal, not a solution assay. Non-degradation entries mean the source measured no significant loss of peptide against a no-enzyme control in a 45 minute assay, which is not proof that no bond can be cleaved. UniProt annotates this protein as mitochondrial as well as cytosolic, and its human catalytic-activity annotation is inferred from the rat orthologue. Reported substrates do not exceed 17 residues.

label: LNPEP / lnpep-observed
training_or_assay: Soluble recombinant human PLAP/IRAP trimming of antigenic peptide precursors, products identified by reverse-phase separation and mass spectrometry (Georgiadou et al. 2010, J Immunol 185:1584-1592)
exposure_requirement: Requires enzyme access in endosome; location does not establish exposure
limitations: Exact-sequence lookup, not a trimming model. The source names this enzyme PLAP; the UniProt gene name is LNPEP and the mouse homolog is called IRAP. Digestions ran at pH 8.0 in Tris buffer with purified enzyme, which is not the acidified endosomal compartment the enzyme is proposed to act in; the paper performs no localization experiment. Reported bonds are those fixed by a single-residue product identity. Where the source detected trimming but no intermediate, cleavage is recorded without a bond rather than assigned to one. Non-detection is that assay's outcome and does not establish resistance elsewhere. The DIRSSVQNKL/DIRSSQVNKL resistant precursor is deliberately excluded pending mhctools issue 332.

label: ERAP1 / eramer-step

limitations: Requires separately fetched ERAMER PWM and openpyxl. Single intermediate score; not a probability, kinetic rate or cascade average. No allotype, enzyme exposure or MHC protection model.
